zebralogic.title: Consolidate Direct Equivalences
zebralogic.principle: When a clue directly equates two or more attribute values (e.g., "the horse keeper drinks Lime smoothies"), merge those values into a single combined entity and propagate the equivalence throughout the puzzle.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue states that two attributes refer to the same person or house.
zebralogic.example: Treating "the horse keeper drinks Lime smoothies" as two separate facts instead of linking horse ↔ Lime smoothie, leading to inconsistent assignments.

zebralogic.title: Assign Fixed Positions Immediately
zebralogic.principle: If a clue pins an attribute to a specific house number, record that placement right away and propagate all consequences before exploring other possibilities.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue contains a house index (e.g., "the third house" or "not in the first house").
zebralogic.example: Delaying the placement of "the black‑haired person is in the third house" can cause later contradictions.

zebralogic.title: Enforce Adjacency for 'next to' and Ordered Left
zebralogic.principle: Adjacency clues ('next to', 'directly left of', 'directly right of') require the two referenced houses to be immediate neighbors.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses the words "next to", "directly left of", or "directly right of".
zebralogic.example: Placing the mountain‑vacation house two houses away from the root‑beer house despite the clue "directly left of".

zebralogic.title: Output Solution in Expected JSON Table Format
zebralogic.principle: The verifier expects a JSON object with a "header" array listing column names and a "rows" array of house entries; any deviation causes a parsing failure.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: At the very end of the response, before any trailing text.
zebralogic.example: Returning the solution as plain text or with missing brackets, causing the verifier to reject the answer.

zebralogic.title: Keep Reasoning Concise to Avoid Token Truncation
zebralogic.principle: The model has a limited token budget; overly long reasoning can cause the final JSON to be cut off, resulting in an invalid answer.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When drafting the explanation, aim for brevity and place the full JSON at the very end.
zebralogic.example: Writing an extensive step‑by‑step narrative that exceeds the token limit, truncating the closing JSON.

zebralogic.title: Preserve Original Attribute Tokens (Case and Spelling)
zebralogic.principle: Attribute values must be reproduced exactly as given (including case, spaces, punctuation); any deviation leads to a mismatch with the reference solution.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When writing the final JSON rows, copy attribute strings verbatim from the puzzle description.
zebralogic.example: Changing "Root Beer" to "rootbeer" or altering capitalization, causing the answer to be rejected.

zebralogic.title: Interpret Directional Ordering Correctly
zebralogic.principle: Clues containing "somewhere to the right of" or "somewhere to the left of" enforce a strict ordering but do not require adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses the phrase "somewhere" together with a direction.
zebralogic.example: Treating "some somewhere left of" as an adjacency constraint, forcing houses to be next to each other incorrectly.

zebralogic.title: Enforce Exclusion Constraints for Specific House Numbers
zebralogic.principle: If a clue forbids an attribute from a particular house (e.g., "the dog owner is not in the fifth house"), record that exclusion immediately and use it to prune possibilities.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue contains "not in house X" or similar negative placement language.
zebralogic.example: Allowing the dog owner to occupy house 5 despite a clue stating it is prohibited.

zebralogic.title: Transitive Ordering Inference
zebralogic.principle: When multiple direct ordering clues form a chain (e.g., A left of B and B left of C), infer the implied ordering (A left of C) to reduce the search space.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: After processing all explicit ordering clues, look for transitive relationships.
zebralogic.example: Missing the inference that if house 1 is left of house 3 and house 3 left of house 5, then house 1 must be left of house 5, leading to unnecessary branching.

zebralogic.title: Distinguish Adjacency vs Ordering in Directional Clues
zebralogic.principle: Treat "directly left/right of" and "next to" as requiring immediate neighboring houses, while "somewhere left/right of" only imposes a relative ordering without adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue contains directional language, first check for the presence of "directly" or "next to" to enforce adjacency; otherwise, apply only ordering constraints.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting "directly left of" as a non‑adjacent ordering, resulting in a gap between the two referenced houses.

zebralogic.description: Generating overly long reasoning before the final answer, causing token truncation.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model continues to elaborate on deductions without accounting for the limited output length, so the JSON solution gets cut off.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Keep the explanatory text brief and place the complete JSON solution at the very end of the response.

zebralogic.description: Providing the solution in a format not recognized by the verifier.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model deviates from the required JSON schema (e.g., missing "header" or "rows", wrong nesting).
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Follow the exact JSON structure: a top‑level object with "header" and "rows" arrays, matching the column order shown in the prompt.

zebralogic.description: Using incorrect case or synonyms for attribute values.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model rewrites attribute strings (e.g., "Root Beer" → "rootbeer") thinking it is harmless, but the verifier checks exact token matches.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Copy attribute values verbatim from the puzzle description; never alter capitalization, spacing, or punctuation.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model confuses "left of" with "right of" or swaps the direction when translating natural language to house indices.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue says "X is left of Y", ensure X's house number is numerically smaller than Y's; similarly for "right of".

zebralogic.description: Treating adjacency clues as non‑adjacent ordering, leading to placement errors.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model applies only a relative ordering constraint to clues that actually require immediate neighbors (e.g., "directly left of").
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Apply the adjacency rule for "directly left/right of" and "next to"; use ordering only for clues with "somewhere".
